evals.prompt: Create a PR on GitHub for my current branch and assign it to me. Do not add reviewers.
evals.expected_output: The workflow creates or updates the PR and assigns the authenticated user without adding a reviewer.
expectations: The workflow checks for an existing PR before creating a new one.
The workflow assigns the authenticated user as assignee.
The workflow does not add the authenticated user or anyone else as reviewer.

evals.prompt: Create a pull request for this branch. I did not specify whether it is ready for review.
evals.expected_output: The workflow creates the PR as a draft by default.
expectations: The workflow creates a new PR as draft when readiness was not specified.
The workflow reports the resulting draft state.
The workflow preserves the state of an existing PR instead of forcing it back to draft.
The workflow does not ask the user to confirm the established draft default.

evals.prompt: Create a ready-for-review PR for this branch and assign it to me.
evals.expected_output: The workflow respects the explicit ready state and assigns the authenticated user.
expectations: The workflow does not apply the draft default.
The workflow assigns the authenticated user as assignee.
The workflow reports that the PR is ready for review.

evals.prompt: Show me the PR title and description in chat. Do not create or update anything on GitHub.
evals.expected_output: The workflow returns copyable English PR content without external changes.
expectations: The output contains the title and complete description in one markdown code block.
All PR content is in English.
The workflow does not create, update, assign, or push a PR.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for a branch with five commits. The last commit only updates tests, while earlier commits contain the feature.
evals.expected_output: The workflow describes the cumulative branch changes rather than only the last commit.
expectations: The workflow fetches the remote default branch and compares its remote-tracking ref with HEAD.
The workflow reviews the full branch diff and commit range.
The title and Summary reflect the feature from all commits rather than only the final test commit.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for my local branch. It has commits but has never been pushed.
evals.expected_output: The workflow publishes the branch before creating the PR.
expectations: The workflow detects that the branch has no upstream.
The workflow pushes the current branch and establishes an upstream.
The workflow creates the PR only after the branch is available remotely.
The workflow does not request separate permission for the push already covered by PR creation.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for this branch, but there is already an open PR from the same branch.
evals.expected_output: The workflow updates the existing PR instead of creating a duplicate.
expectations: The workflow finds the existing PR for the current branch.
The workflow updates that PR instead of creating another one.
The workflow preserves unrelated metadata and the existing draft state.

evals.prompt: Create a PR. The branch fixes a duplicate focus event and adds a regression test. I ran pnpm test and pnpm lint locally, but do not put those commands in the description.
evals.expected_output: The PR body focuses on the duplicate-event fix without a routine test bullet, testing-only section, or local command list.
expectations: The workflow does not add a Testing, Tests, Validation, Verification, Local verification, QA, or similar section.
The workflow does not list pnpm test or pnpm lint in the PR body.
The Summary describes the duplicate-event fix without a standalone bullet for the regression test.

evals.prompt: Generate PR content for a dependency branch that updates vitest 4.1.9 to 4.1.10 and @vitest/ui 4.1.9 to 4.1.10.
evals.expected_output: The PR description lists every changed dependency and both versions.
expectations: The description includes a separate entry for vitest with both versions.
The description includes a separate entry for @vitest/ui with both versions.
The description does not replace the package details with a vague dependency-update statement.

evals.prompt: Create a PR description from this refactor. We have no issue, user research, performance measurements, or migration requirement.
evals.expected_output: The PR content stays energetic but does not invent unsupported context.
expectations: The Summary uses concrete facts from the branch with an energetic emoji-heavy tone.
The description follows the concrete style reference instead of relying only on abstract style adjectives.
The description does not invent issue references, user demand, metrics, motivation, or future plans.
The description omits unsupported optional sections.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for this feature branch. The commit-creator skill is installed. The current task changed src/status.ts and its test, and neither file is committed. docs/other-task.md is staged for unrelated work. Preserve that other work.
evals.expected_output: The agent commits only the task changes, publishes the branch, and creates a draft PR while preserving the unrelated staged work.
expectations: The workflow follows commit-creator to create an English conventional task commit.
The workflow preserves unrelated staged and unstaged changes.
The workflow performs the necessary commit and push without repeated authorization questions.
The workflow creates the PR only after its branch changes are published.

evals.prompt: The PR you created earlier is complete. Now adjust one label and run the relevant check; I have not asked for a new publication.
evals.expected_output: The agent edits and verifies without treating the completed PR request as continuing authorization to commit, push, or update the PR.
expectations: The workflow keeps this new work local.
The workflow does not infer new publication authorization from the earlier completed request.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for the current task. I am on main, matching the fresh origin/main. src/status.ts and its test contain uncommitted task changes. docs/other-task.md is staged for unrelated work. The project uses feature/ branch names.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a task branch before committing, then commits and publishes only the task changes and creates the PR.
expectations: The workflow creates and switches to a branch following the feature/ convention before making a task commit.
The workflow preserves unrelated changes and their staging state.
The workflow completes commit, push, and PR creation without stopping solely because it started on main or asking for repeated authorization.

evals.prompt: I am on main, matching origin/main, with uncommitted changes for the status label. Give me the PR title and description in chat based on those changes.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the working-tree diff to produce copyable PR content while keeping the current branch and Git state.
expectations: The workflow reads the uncommitted changes instead of stopping because main has no commits ahead of the base.
The workflow keeps the current branch and creates no branch, commit, push, or GitHub PR.
The output distinguishes uncommitted work from published branch changes.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for the current feature branch. Only pr-creator is installed. The repository commit instructions require an English conventional message and preserving unrelated staging. src/status.ts has uncommitted task changes and docs/other-task.md is staged for unrelated work. The branch also contains a previous commit that has not been checked for this task.
evals.expected_output: The agent follows the repository commit instructions, preserves staging, and inspects every outgoing commit before pushing.
expectations: The workflow uses the repository commit instructions when commit-creator is unavailable.
The workflow preserves unrelated staged changes.
The workflow checks the full outgoing changeset before push and resolves unrelated or unclear committed scope before publication.

evals.prompt: Draft a PR on GitHub for the current feature branch. Its task changes are committed, verified, and pushed, and there is no existing PR.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a draft PR on GitHub without asking whether the user wanted chat text.
expectations: The workflow creates a GitHub draft, not only copyable chat content.
The workflow preserves the draft default and does not request redundant publication authorization.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for feat/gh-42-session-cache in acme/app. This is a new session with no task discussion. The branch changes are verified and pushed. The configured tracker is GitHub Issues in this repository, and the tracker API is available.
evals.expected_output: The agent retrieves issue #42, compares its requirements and comments with the complete branch diff, and adds a closing reference when all requirements are met without asking the user to identify the task again.
expectations: The agent reads acme/app issue #42 rather than relying on the branch name as proof of completion.
When the changes meet all requirements, the PR body contains Closes #42 or another supported closing keyword.
The agent does not ask for redundant confirmation of the matching task.
The agent reads back the published PR and checks its intended closing reference.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for feat/gh-42-session-cache in acme/app. Issue #42 requires caching, invalidation after logout, and concurrent refresh handling. The branch adds caching, but logout and refresh handling are unchanged. This PR is the first part of that task.
evals.expected_output: The PR references #42 without closing it and states the remaining requirements.
expectations: The agent uses a non-closing reference and identifies logout invalidation and concurrent refresh handling as remaining work.
The agent does not add a closing keyword or a Development closing link for #42.
The agent does not claim that the branch ID proves full completion.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for fix/APP-123-token-refresh. The project uses Jira at https://acme.atlassian.net and has a GitHub integration. APP-123 requires rejecting expired refresh tokens; the branch implements this requirement. No Jira status automation has been confirmed.
evals.expected_output: The agent verifies APP-123 and includes its key and URL without promising an unverified status transition.
expectations: The agent reads APP-123 and compares its requirements with the branch changes.
The PR description includes APP-123 and its Jira URL, not a GitHub closing reference for issue #123.
The agent preserves the key case and does not add a task ID to the PR title.
The agent does not change the Jira status or claim it will close automatically.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for fix/gh-42-token-refresh in acme/app. The tracker request for acme/app#42 returns 403 Forbidden. The branch diff rejects expired refresh tokens.
evals.expected_output: The agent reports the unavailable task evidence and asks for the missing context before choosing a closing reference.
expectations: The agent does not infer the contents or completion of #42 from the branch name.
The agent asks a specific question about the inaccessible task while continuing independent PR preparation.
The agent does not silently claim or publish a verified closing relationship.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for the current branch in acme/app. The configured task tracker is acme/backlog. A commit body contains Refs acme/backlog#42. That issue requests the complete behavior implemented by this branch, and the tracker API is available.
evals.expected_output: The agent recovers the cross-repository task from the full commit message and uses a qualified closing reference.
expectations: The agent reads complete commit messages and retrieves acme/backlog#42.
The PR uses Closes acme/backlog#42 or another supported qualified closing keyword.
The agent does not replace the task with acme/app#42 or a bare #42.

evals.prompt: Update the existing PR from feat/gh-42-session-cache. It targets release/2.x, while main is the default branch. Issue #42 is fully addressed. Keep the PR target and ready state unchanged.
evals.expected_output: The agent keeps the requested metadata and uses a normal task reference without promising closure from merging into release/2.x.
expectations: The agent preserves release/2.x and the existing ready state.
The description references #42 without promising automatic closure on this merge.
The agent does not close #42 directly.

evals.prompt: Create a PR for GitHub issue acme/app#42 from my changes on main. The project uses fix/ branch names. The changes fully meet the issue requirements, which are available through the tracker API. The commit-creator skill is installed.
evals.expected_output: The agent creates a task branch with the known ID, uses commit-creator for the commit, verifies the task, and publishes the PR with a closing reference.
expectations: The new branch follows fix/ and includes the GitHub issue ID.
The agent follows commit-creator for the task commit.
The agent verifies #42 and adds the closing reference without requiring implementation-workflow.
The agent commits, pushes, and creates the draft PR without repeated authorization questions.

evals.prompt: Prepare the PR title and description for fix/gh-42-refresh-expiry. This session already contains a complete analysis of every branch commit and changed file, issue #42 requirements and comments, and passing required checks. Fresh Git state confirms the same base and head commits and an unchanged clean working tree. The changes fully resolve #42 and target the default branch. Do not publish anything.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the existing complete analysis and task evidence to produce PR content with a closing reference, without a second full review or check run.
expectations: The PR body includes a supported closing reference to #42.
The agent reuses the matching complete changeset analysis and already-read issue context.
The agent does not repeat the full code inspection or rerun passing checks solely to choose the task reference.
The agent keeps the action text-only.
